text: The paper's claims were stress-tested in a nineteen-round adversarial protocol in which three frontier language models, under the author's direction, alternately attempted to identify counterexamples, algebraic errors, and overstatements; the surviving statements are those neither system broke.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Refundable Stake Does Not Expand Deterrent Capacity in Long-Lived Delegation: Collateral, Premia, and Pseudonymous Markets (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7322599

isBasedOn.name: Refundable Stake Does Not Expand Deterrent Capacity in Long-Lived Delegation: Collateral, Premia, and Pseudonymous Markets

abstract: After the author’s initial formulation, the claims below were stress- tested in a nineteen-round adversarial protocol in which three frontier language models (Claude, Grok and Codex), under the author’s direction, alternately attempted to identify counterexamples, algebraic errors, and overstatements. The surviving statements are those that neither system broke, and the audit trail is preserved in the author’s research archive.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: the audit protocol is neither peer review nor a substitute for complete formal proofs
